content.text: Instead of deciding on a new hardcoded property which to map F3 PIDs to, would it be more flexible to instead introduce a configuration element (with a default of "dc:identifier") that can be changed to whatever the user wants?
That sounds more flexible.  We should change the default though as well, to avoid a collision between the dc:identifiers from the fedora 3 DC datastream and the dc:identifier from the pid.
To be clear, we weren't explicitly migrating the PID before, we were relying on the behavior of fedora 3 where the pid is automatically populated in the DC datastream.  This

Thanks for the clarifying notes and the plan. Have you landed on a reasonable default property for the F3 PID to migrate to? If not, maybe a note to fedora-tech is in order.

comments.body: Instead of deciding on a new hardcoded property which to map F3 PIDs to, would it be more flexible to instead introduce a configuration element (with a default of "dc:identifier") that can be changed to whatever the user wants?
That sounds more flexible. We should change the default though as well, to avoid a collision between the dc:identifiers from the fedora 3 DC datastream and the dc:identifier from the pid.

To be clear, we weren't explicitly migrating the PID before, we were relying on the behavior of fedora 3 where the pid is automatically populated in the DC datastream. This may not have been a safe assumption, because perhaps you can delete that from the DC datastream, furthermore, as the issue reporter pointed out, there's no automatic way to discern the pid among potentially multiple dc:identifier fields.

This fix will:
1. explicitly migrate the pid
2. allow users to set a custom predicate for that (and other simple) property
Thanks for the clarifying notes and the plan. Have you landed on a reasonable default property for the F3 PID to migrate to? If not, maybe a note to fedora-tech is in order.
Looks good, pending response to code review comment.
